title: Did you see it, or hear it?
goal: Choose -dY for what you saw and -(Y)pdYr for what you found out or heard.

intro.text: Saw it happen, or simply know it: `-dY`, *Gije gar ýagdy*. Found it out from the result, or heard it: `-(Y)pdYr`, *Gije gar ýagypdyr!* (you wake up and everything is white). News you pass on comes in `-(Y)pdYr`: *Eşitdiňmi? Merdan öýlenipdir!*

exercises.question: You wake up and everything outside is white. What do you say?

why.1: *ýagdy* is what you'd say if you had watched it fall.

exercises.explain: You see the result, not the snowfall: *ýagypdyr*.

exercises.question: You watched your little brother knock the glass off the table. What do you tell your mother?

why.1: *döwüpdir* would mean you only found the pieces, or someone told you.

exercises.explain: You saw it: the plain past, *döwdi*.

exercises.text: Merjen Mara ___, men ony wokzalda gördüm. Aýna hem ___, goňşy aýtdy.
exercises.en: Merjen went to Mary; I saw her at the station. Aýna has gone too, the neighbour said.
exercises.explain: You saw Merjen leave: *gitdi*. You only heard about Aýna: *gidipdir*.

accept: Have you heard? Merdan got married!
Did you hear? Merdan [got married|has got married|has gotten married]!
Have you heard? Merdan [has got married|has gotten married]!

exercises.prompt: Someone has broken the glass! (You find the pieces on the floor.)
accept: Biri stakany döwüpdir!

reject.why: You didn't see it happen; you found the pieces: *döwüpdir*.

exercises.explain: *biri*, someone; *döw-* + *-üp* + *-dir*: has broken, as you can see.

exercises.question: You phone Merdan's home. His mother says he left an hour ago. What do you tell Aýna?

why.1: *gitdi* sounds as if you saw him leave.

exercises.explain: You heard it from his mother: *gidipdir*.

exercises.prompt: Men oňa jaň etdim, ýöne ol eýýäm gidipdir.
accept: I called him, but he had already left.
I phoned [him|her], but [he|she] had already [left|gone].
I called her, but she had already [left|gone].
I called him, but he had already gone.
I called him, but he had already left, it turned out.
I called him, but it turned out he had already left.

exercises.label: *gitmek* with `-(Y)pdYr`, question: have I gone?, have you gone?…

accept: gidipdirinmi
gidipmisiň
gidipdirmi
gidipdirismi
gidipmisiňiz
gidipdirlermi
gidipdirmi

exercises.explain: The particle goes at the end, except with **you**, where it comes before the ending: *gidipmisiň?*

exercises.text: The neighbour said it rained at night.

accept: Sen täzeligi eşitdiňmi?
Täzeligi eşitdiňmi?
(Siz) täzeligi eşitdiňizmi?

reject.why: *täzelik* ends in *k* and has three syllables: before a vowel the *k* becomes *g*, *täzeligi*.

exercises.question: Which sentence tells something the speaker saw for themselves?

why.1: *gidipdir*: you know it from someone else, or from what you see now.
why.2: *eken*: you have just found it out or heard it.

exercises.explain: *gördüm*, I saw: the plain past for what you witnessed.

exercises.prompt: Bu şäherde öň gadymy bir gala bolupdyr.
accept: There was once an ancient fortress in this town.
Long ago there was an ancient fortress in this town.
There used to be an ancient fortress in this town.
There was an ancient fortress in this town before.
There was once an ancient fortress in this city.
There used to be an ancient fortress in this city, they say.

exercises.en: I came home: Mum has made palaw!

accept: ipdir

reject.why: You weren't there when she cooked it; you find it ready: *bişiripdir*.
*bişirýär* is **she's cooking** now. You find it already made: *bişiripdir*.

exercises.explain: *bişir-* + *-ip* + *-dir*: *bişiripdir*, she has made it, as you see.
